claims.statement: Authorities must accept compliant electronic freight information from 9 July 2027, while businesses are not required by the eFTI Regulation to choose electronic presentation.
The statutory definition of eFTI service includes processing by means of an eFTI platform alone or with other ICT solutions, and contractual service providers are certified under Article 13.
A direct-to-operator adapter cannot safely assume that certification is delegated merely because an upstream platform is certified.
The platform requirements reuse source data from TMS and ERP systems and require controlled authorisation, strong authentication, security, auditability, and authority access.
A public developer portal exposes API schemas and interoperability-test guidance, reducing pure protocol-discovery risk.
TransFollow and Ybil already target TMS vendors with open or plug-in APIs and report dozens of integrations; Shippeo also integrates eCMR by API.
The white space, if any, is a Polish legacy-schema component embedded inside a certified partner, rather than a generic eFTI API.
The reviewed sources do not establish a Polish TMS budget, upstream wholesale fee, or willingness to pay for a multi-platform adapter.
A part-time prototype is technically compatible with the founder, but enterprise security diligence and production support are not demonstrated as part-time-compatible.

contrary_evidence: Paper remains a lawful substitute for operators after the authority-acceptance date.
A contractual adapter provider may itself fall within the certified eFTI service-provider perimeter.
Direct competitors already sell API integrations to TMS and ERP vendors and possess installed networks.
Shippeo states that certification processes are not fully available yet, while the Commission schedules remaining specifications for December 2026.
Official market data indicate weaker use of APIs and digital consignment notes among smaller freight firms than of more established tools.
